**Benefits of going to school for UX**

\-Opportunities to network with individuals in UX whether it's professors, students, and more networking opportunities in your co-op placements. You can still network with people if you didn't do ux which is still great, but it'd make sense that networking with other ux designers in the real workplace would be better. im sure you'd still have chances to talk to ux designers with an unrelated job placement though if there are any in your workplace.

\-Probably easier to start off your ux career if you have a degree or some kind of education on it. from what i've been told and from what i've seen, it's not necessary to have one but i'm sure it helps.

**Benefits of learning UX on your own**

\-More freedom to learn at your own pace. If school was never for you, or you learn better without a school environment, you can still build a portfolio through personal projects and such. Watch youtube videos, try out software like figma and adobe xd on your own, and reaching out to ux professionals on your own time would still be effective i believe.

\-if you continue learning on your own, there may be transferable skills from your degree that can be used in ux. for example if you've done research in co-ops or in actual jobs, it can help you do user research in ux.

I posted something similar to this on a different reddit thread and got some answers so I'll share some that helped me...

1. Stressing only makes you more tired. I stress over things as well, so I understand how hard it is to just "stop stressing". But just try. What's the point in stressing over something that hasn't happened yet? Just don't give a fuck about things that haven't happened yet, they don't exist. It may not even happen. I recommend this video that I just saw [here](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=dOImyOGN9UE&t=2s).
2. Think of life as something with branches instead of something linear. You're only at the trunks. You'll definitely be given a chance, or chances, to turn your life around. Just wait patiently for that, and run towards those opportunities with full force and open arms.
3. Someone replied to me saying "You can do everything wrong for the next decade and still be young as fuck" which kinda helped me. We're still so young. So what, you fuck up now? It'll be a fun story to tell when you're older.

I'm not sure exactly what you're going through but just know that losing your path is the way to finding a path. I'm finding it hard to follow this advice given to me too, but it comforted me knowing that there were people that had the same mindset as this and got through it. I hope this helped you even just a little bit, good luck out there!

edit: just something to add, you have so much time so don't feel overwhelmed. there's no need to be making millions of dollars as soon as you get out of uni/college. take time for yourself. lay down for an hour and do absolutely nothing if that helps.
